_comment: Edit this list to match your trees. chill_hours_min/max are nursery-style chill hour ratings (hours between 32 and 45 F, Oct 1 - Mar 31). cold_damage_f is the winter low that starts to injure wood or buds; cold_kill_f is where serious damage or top-kill is likely. bloom_risk says how exposed the bloom is to spring frost.

trees.name: Sweet cherry (Bing / Rainier type)
trees.notes: Blooms early to mid April here. At full bloom, 28°F kills about 10% of flowers and 25°F about 90%.

trees.name: Italian prune plum (European)
trees.notes: Late bloomer, so spring frost is rarely a problem.

trees.name: Beauty plum (Japanese)
trees.notes: Low chill, so it is ready to bloom by midwinter and flowers at the first warm spell. Late-March and April freezes are its main threat.

trees.name: Fig (hardy type, e.g. Chicago Hardy)
trees.notes: Chill is never the issue here; winter cold is. Branches start to die back around 15°F and the top usually dies to the ground near 5°F, though the roots of hardy types regrow.
